'''Todd Benjamin Heap''' (born March 16, 1980) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[tight end]] for 12 seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL), primarily for the [[Baltimore Ravens]].  He was selected to the [[Pro Bowl]] twice with the Ravens, earning second-team [[All-Pro]] honors in 2003.

After playing [[college football]] for the [[Arizona State Sun Devils football|Arizona State Sun Devils]], Heap was selected by Baltimore in the first round of the [[2001 NFL draft]]. He played ten years for the Ravens, becoming the franchise's all-time leader in [[touchdown]] catches and second all-time in [[Reception (gridiron football)|receptions]] and yards. He played two years for the [[Arizona Cardinals]] from 2011-2012.<ref name="Downing">{{cite web |last=Downing |first=Garrett |title=Todd Heap Going Into Ravens Ring of Honor |url=http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Todd-Heap-Going-Into-Ravens-Ring-of-Honor/76032649-c70c-43a8-851e-0a5913a42f14 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514163803/http://www.baltimoreravens.com/news/article-1/Todd-Heap-Going-Into-Ravens-Ring-of-Honor/76032649-c70c-43a8-851e-0a5913a42f14 |archive-date=May 14, 2014 |access-date=May 14, 2014 |website=BaltimoreRavens.com |publisher=}}</ref>

'''Todd Merlin McMillon''' (born September 26, 1974) is an American former professional [[gridiron football|football]] player who was a [[cornerback]] for the [[Chicago Bears]] of the [[National Football League]] (NFL).<ref>[http://www.nfl.com/players/toddmcmillon/profile?id=MCM685460 NFL Stats]. Retrieved December 29, 2010</ref>  He played [[college football]] for the [[Northern Arizona Lumberjacks football|Northern Arizona Lumberjacks]] before being signed as an [[undrafted free agent]].<ref>[http://campblitz.wordpress.com/about/ Camp Blitz]. Retrieved December 29, 2010</ref>  He also spent three years with the [[Saskatchewan Roughriders]] of the [[Canadian Football League|CFL]].<ref>[http://www.combines.com/alumni/spotlight.asp?playerid=11 Pro Football Combine Profile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100820201907/http://www.combines.com/alumni/spotlight.asp?playerid=11 |date=August 20, 2010 }}. Retrieved December 29, 2010</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.profootballarchives.com/playerm/mcmi03600.html|title = Todd McMillon Stats - Pro Football Archives}}</ref> In 2001, he played for the [[Frankfurt Galaxy (NFL Europe)|Frankfurt Galaxy]] of [[NFL Europe]] and earned NFL Europe All-Pro honors.<ref name="Bears">{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20050308164550/http://www.chicagobears.com/team/teamRosterDetails.jsp?id=424|archivedate=March 8, 2005|title=Todd McMillon|publisher=Chicago Bears|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/team/teamRosterDetails.jsp?id|accessdate=October 11, 2020|url-status=dead}}</ref>

McMillon [[Model (person)|models]] for such retailers as the [[Gap (clothing retailer)|GAP]] in his spare time, which has earned him the nickname "Runway" with his teammates.<ref>[http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_m1208/is_24_229/ai_n13812571/ Inside the NFC]. Retrieved December 29, 2010</ref>  He also appeared on an episode of ''Teammates'' on [[ESPN]] with teammate [[Brian Urlacher]].<ref>[http://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/teammates-2005/episode-5-season-1/teammates/204802 TV Guide]. Retrieved December 29, 2010</ref>

In June 2013, McMillon was told by his doctor that he had [[prostate cancer]], and stated, "When he told me I was positive for cancer, I just went numb. I thought he had the wrong test. I played in the NFL. I am super healthy. I work out all the time, so I am in really good shape. I was like, 'This can't be me. I'm only 39 and I have prostate cancer?'" In August, McMillon had his [[prostate]] removed, which had contained the disease.<ref>{{cite web|last=Mayer|first=Larry|url=http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/McMillon-raising-cancer-awareness/39e69f3d-55b5-4956-a5e4-8db8c3b1b343|title=McMillon raising cancer awareness|publisher=[[Chicago Bears]]|date=January 30, 2014|accessdate=January 30, 2014|archive-date=February 4, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140204055731/http://www.chicagobears.com/news/article-1/McMillon-raising-cancer-awareness/39e69f3d-55b5-4956-a5e4-8db8c3b1b343|url-status=dead}}</ref>

'''Tobin Bo Gunnar Gerhart''' (born March 28, 1987) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[running back]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Stanford Cardinal football|Stanford Cardinal]], earning [[unanimous All-American]] honors. He was selected by the [[Minnesota Vikings]] in the second round of the [[2010 NFL draft]]. With Stanford in [[2009 Stanford Cardinal football team|2009]], Gerhart won the [[Doak Walker Award]]<ref name="CBS Sports ranking">{{Citation |url=http://www.cbssports.com/nfl/draft/prospectrankings/TSX/2010_RB |title=2010 NFL Draft RB ranking |work=CBS Sports |access-date=February 8, 2010 }}</ref> and was the runner-up for the 2009 [[Heisman Trophy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=December 7, 2009 |title=McCoy among five finalists for Heisman |url=https://www.espn.com/college-football/news/story?id=4723007 |access-date=December 7, 2009 |website=[[ESPN.com]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}}</ref>  He received 1,276 points in the Heisman voting, coming in second to [[Mark Ingram II]], who received 1,304 points; the 28-point margin is the closest vote in Heisman history.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/football/news?slug=ap-heismantrophy&prov=ap&type=lgns |publisher=[[rivals.com]] |access-date=December 13, 2009 |title=Ingram delivers Alabama its first Heisman }}{{dead link|date=December 2016 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>  Gerhart had a breakout senior season in 2009, leading all running backs in the nation in rushing yards, touchdowns, and points scored, and setting several Pac-10 and school [[Toby Gerhart#Records|records]].  He held the Stanford record for most rushing yards in a season (1,871) until [[Christian McCaffrey]] broke it in 2015, and still holds Cardinal records for touchdowns in a season (28) and most touchdowns in a career (44).

Collins was a champion in [[High school football|high school]] and [[College football|college]] football. He led Jefferson County High School to the 1987 [[TSSAA]] AAA State Championship. Coming out of Jefferson County, Collins was a ''[[USA Today]]'' High School [[All-America]]n. He received a [[scholarship]] to the [[Georgia Bulldogs football|University of Georgia]], where his older brother Brent was already enrolled. Injury problems kept Todd off the field during the 1988 season, and he transferred to the [[Tennessee Volunteers football|University of Tennessee]] for one semester. Both Collins brothers subsequently ended up at [[Carson–Newman Eagles football|Carson-Newman College]], with whom they won the 1989 [[National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics|NAIA]] National Championship.

'''Tobias Williams''' (born November 19, 1959) is an American former professional [[American football|football]] player who was a [[defensive lineman]] in the [[National Football League]] (NFL). He played [[college football]] for the [[Nebraska Cornhuskers football|Nebraska Cornhuskers]] and was selected by the [[New York Jets]] in the 10th round of the [[1983 NFL draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1983 NFL Draft Listing |url=https://www.pro-football-reference.com/years/1983/draft.htm |access-date=February 5, 2023 |website=Pro-Football-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played six seasons, as a defensive end and defensive tackle, all with the [[New England Patriots]].

The 1987 season was interrupted by a [[1987 NFL Players Strike#1987 strike and decertification|labor dispute]].  Soon after the strike began, the Patriots coaching staff accused Williams of throwing a beer bottle at [[strikebreaker|replacement players]] during a confrontation at a union picket line.<ref name="globe-confrontation">Boston Globe; September 25, 1987</ref> Williams missed training camp the next summer; the Patriots retained his rights but they gave him permission to negotiate with other teams. He signed with the Patriots just before the season began.<ref name="globe-contract">The Boston Globe; August 27, 1988</ref> He retired from professional football after that [[1988 New England Patriots season|1988 season]].

Since the mid-1990s, he has been an assistant coach at several high schools in suburban Boston, as well as at [[Bridgewater State College]], [[Dean College]] and the [[University at Buffalo]].<ref name="buffalo-bio">{{Cite web |url=http://www.ubathletics.buffalo.edu/football/news/ftb05-03-2006-williams.shtml |title=Archived copy |access-date=December 24, 2009 |archive-date=July 14, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100714174311/http://www.ubathletics.buffalo.edu/football/news/ftb05-03-2006-williams.shtml |url-status=dead }}</ref>

His daughter Candace Williams was a star college basketball player with the [[University of New Hampshire Wildcats]] through the 2009-10 season.
